title: Filter Senior Applicants with 5+ Years Experience
description_markdown: Recruiting request: Find applicants in `applicants` who have at least 5 years of experience (`years_experience >= 5`). Return `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, and `years_experience`. Order by `years_experience` DESC, `first_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Experienced applicants
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT first_name, last_name, email, years_experience FROM applicants WHERE years_experience >= 5 ORDER BY years_experience DESC, first_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Filters the applicant tracking pipeline for senior profiles.
hints: Use `WHERE years_experience >= 5`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT first_name, last_name, email, years_experience FROM applicants WHERE years_experience >= 5 ORDER BY years_experience DESC, first_name ASC;

title: Calculate Average Candidate Interview Scores per Job
description_markdown: Hiring committee request: For each job posting in `job_postings`, calculate the average interviewer score (`ROUND(AVG(interviewer_score), 2)` as `avg_score`) across all interview stages. Return `jp.title`, `jp.department`, and `avg_score`. Order by `avg_score` DESC, `jp.posting_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Average interview score per posting
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT jp.title, jp.department, ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2) AS avg_score FROM job_postings jp JOIN interview_stages i ON jp.posting_id = i.posting_id GROUP BY jp.posting_id, jp.title, jp.department ORDER BY avg_score DESC, jp.posting_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates rubric scores from candidate interview loops.
hints: Join job_postings to interview_stages and group by posting.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT jp.title, jp.department, ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2) AS avg_score FROM job_postings jp JOIN interview_stages i ON jp.posting_id = i.posting_id GROUP BY jp.posting_id, jp.title, jp.department ORDER BY avg_score DESC, jp.posting_id ASC;

title: Audit Accepted Job Offers Against Budget Cap
description_markdown: Compensation review: Join `job_offers`, `job_postings`, and `applicants`. For accepted offers (`job_offers.status = 'accepted'`), calculate how close the offered salary was to the maximum base budget: `(jp.base_salary_max - jo.offered_salary)` as `budget_savings`. Return `a.first_name`, `jp.title`, `jo.offered_salary`, and `budget_savings`. Order by `budget_savings` DESC, `a.applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Accepted offers audit
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT a.first_name, jp.title, jo.offered_salary, (jp.base_salary_max - jo.offered_salary) AS budget_savings FROM job_offers jo JOIN job_postings jp ON jo.posting_id = jp.posting_id JOIN applicants a ON jo.applicant_id = a.applicant_id WHERE jo.status = 'accepted' ORDER BY budget_savings DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Audits final agreed employment compensation versus initial salary band authorization.
hints: Join job_offers -> job_postings -> applicants with status = 'accepted'.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT a.first_name, jp.title, jo.offered_salary, (jp.base_salary_max - jo.offered_salary) AS budget_savings FROM job_offers jo JOIN job_postings jp ON jo.posting_id = jp.posting_id JOIN applicants a ON jo.applicant_id = a.applicant_id WHERE jo.status = 'accepted' ORDER BY budget_savings DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;

description_markdown: Compensation planning: For each department in `job_postings`, count open job requisitions (`COUNT(posting_id)` as `openings_count`) and compute the average salary ceiling (`ROUND(AVG(base_salary_max), 2)` as `avg_salary`). title: Categorize Job Requisitions by Seniority Experience Band
description_markdown:
Classify job postings in `job_postings` into career seniority bands using `CASE` as `seniority_tier`:
- If `min_experience_years >= 7`, return `'Principal/Staff'`
- Else if `min_experience_years >= 5`, return `'Senior'`
- Otherwise, return `'Mid-Level'`

Return `posting_id`, `title`, `min_experience_years`, and `seniority_tier`. Order by `min_experience_years` DESC, `posting_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT posting_id, title, min_experience_years, CASE WHEN min_experience_years >= 7 THEN 'Principal/Staff' WHEN min_experience_years >= 5 THEN 'Senior' ELSE 'Mid-Level' END AS seniority_tier FROM job_postings ORDER BY min_experience_years DESC, posting_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies conditional evaluation to required experience.
hints: Use `CASE WHEN min_experience_years >= 7 THEN 'Principal/Staff' WHEN min_experience_years >= 5 THEN 'Senior' ELSE 'Mid-Level' END`.
Order by `min_experience_years` DESC, `posting_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT posting_id, title, min_experience_years, CASE WHEN min_experience_years >= 7 THEN 'Principal/Staff' WHEN min_experience_years >= 5 THEN 'Senior' ELSE 'Mid-Level' END AS seniority_tier FROM job_postings ORDER BY min_experience_years DESC, posting_id ASC;

title: Join Interview Evaluations with Candidate and Requisition Names
description_markdown: Build an interview tracking ledger by joining `interview_stages`, `applicants`, and `job_postings`. Return `i.stage_id`, `a.first_name`, `a.last_name`, `jp.title`, `i.stage_name`, and `i.interviewer_score`. Order by `i.stage_id` ASC.

solution_explanation: Three-table inner join relating candidates, interview evaluations, and requisitions.

Order by `i.stage_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT i.stage_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, jp.title, i.stage_name, i.interviewer_score FROM interview_stages i JOIN applicants a ON i.applicant_id = a.applicant_id JOIN job_postings jp ON i.posting_id = jp.posting_id ORDER BY i.stage_id ASC;

title: Aggregate Company-Wide Offer Volume and Payroll Commitments

starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT COUNT(offer_id) AS total_offers, SUM(offered_salary) AS total_payroll_offered, ROUND(AVG(offered_salary), 2) AS avg_offered_salary FROM job_offers;
solution_explanation: Aggregates offer count, sum, and average across all job offers.
hints: Use `COUNT(offer_id)`, `SUM(offered_salary)`, and `ROUND(AVG(offered_salary), 2)`.

Query: SELECT COUNT(offer_id) AS total_offers, SUM(offered_salary) AS total_payroll_offered, ROUND(AVG(offered_salary), 2) AS avg_offered_salary FROM job_offers;

title: Calculate Applicant Experience Surplus Over Requisition Minimum
description_markdown: Competency qualification check: For candidates interviewing for positions, calculate the experience surplus above the role's requirement: `(a.years_experience - jp.min_experience_years)` as `experience_surplus`. Return distinct records with `a.applicant_id`, `a.first_name`, `jp.title`, `a.years_experience`, `jp.min_experience_years`, and `experience_surplus`. Order by `experience_surplus` DESC, `a.applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT DISTINCT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, jp.title, a.years_experience, jp.min_experience_years, (a.years_experience - jp.min_experience_years) AS experience_surplus FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id JOIN job_postings jp ON i.posting_id = jp.posting_id ORDER BY experience_surplus DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Computes differential between candidate experience and role prerequisites.
hints: Join `applicants`, `interview_stages`, and `job_postings`.
Compute `(a.years_experience - jp.min_experience_years)` as `experience_surplus`.

Query: SELECT DISTINCT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, jp.title, a.years_experience, jp.min_experience_years, (a.years_experience - jp.min_experience_years) AS experience_surplus FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id JOIN job_postings jp ON i.posting_id = jp.posting_id ORDER BY experience_surplus DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;

title: Compute Aggregate Candidate Interview Performance
description_markdown: Candidate scorecard: For each applicant who has gone through interviews, calculate total rounds completed (`COUNT(i.stage_id)` as `total_stages`) and their overall mean score (`ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2)` as `candidate_avg_score`). title: Calculate Offered Compensation Share of Budget Band Ceiling
description_markdown: Compensation fairness review: For each record in `job_offers`, compute what percentage of the role's maximum base salary was offered: `ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 100.0) / jp.base_salary_max, 2)` as `pct_of_budget`. Return `jo.offer_id`, `jp.title`, `jo.offered_salary`, `jp.base_salary_max`, and `pct_of_budget`. Order by `pct_of_budget` DESC, `jo.offer_id` ASC.

solution_explanation: Compares offered compensation package to departmental max budget ceiling.
hints: Compute `ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 100.0) / jp.base_salary_max, 2)`.
Join on `jo.posting_id = jp.posting_id`.

Query: SELECT jo.offer_id, jp.title, jo.offered_salary, jp.base_salary_max, ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 100.0) / jp.base_salary_max, 2) AS pct_of_budget FROM job_offers jo JOIN job_postings jp ON jo.posting_id = jp.posting_id ORDER BY pct_of_budget DESC, jo.offer_id ASC;

title: Identify Top Scoring Interview Stage per Candidate
description_markdown: Using `ROW_NUMBER()`, retrieve the single highest-scoring interview stage completed by each candidate. If scores tie, select the lowest `stage_id`. Return `applicant_id`, `posting_id`, `stage_name`, and `interviewer_score`. Order by `applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH TopStages AS (SELECT applicant_id, posting_id, stage_name, interviewer_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY applicant_id ORDER BY interviewer_score DESC, stage_id ASC) AS rn FROM interview_stages) SELECT applicant_id, posting_id, stage_name, interviewer_score FROM TopStages WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by applicant to find their highest rating.
hints: Use `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY applicant_id ORDER BY interviewer_score DESC, stage_id ASC)` in a CTE.
Filter outer query with `WHERE rn = 1`.

Query: WITH TopStages AS (SELECT applicant_id, posting_id, stage_name, interviewer_score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY applicant_id ORDER BY interviewer_score DESC, stage_id ASC) AS rn FROM interview_stages) SELECT applicant_id, posting_id, stage_name, interviewer_score FROM TopStages WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY applicant_id ASC;

title: Dense Rank Candidate Pool by Years of Industry Experience
description_markdown: Rank all candidates in `applicants` by `years_experience` descending using `DENSE_RANK()` as `exp_rank`. Return `applicant_id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `years_experience`, and `exp_rank`. Order by `exp_rank` ASC, `applicant_id` ASC.

solution_explanation: Applies DENSE_RANK window function ordered by years of experience.

Order by `exp_rank` ASC, `applicant_id` ASC.
Query: SELECT applicant_id, first_name, last_name, years_experience, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY years_experience DESC) AS exp_rank FROM applicants ORDER BY exp_rank ASC, applicant_id ASC;

title: Filter Requisitions Exceeding Company Mean Base Salary
description_markdown: Filter job requisitions in `job_postings` whose salary ceiling is strictly greater than the average maximum base salary across all job postings. Return `posting_id`, `title`, `department`, and `base_salary_max`. Order by `base_salary_max` DESC, `posting_id` ASC.

title: Track Previous Interview Round Score with Window LAG

solution_query: SELECT stage_id, applicant_id, stage_name, interviewer_score, completed_at, LAG(interviewer_score) OVER (PARTITION BY applicant_id ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC) AS prev_score FROM interview_stages ORDER BY applicant_id ASC, completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies LAG window function over candidate interview timelines.
hints: Use `LAG(interviewer_score) OVER (PARTITION BY applicant_id ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC)`.

title: Count Candidates Evaluated per Job Requisition

title: Count Extended and Accepted Job Offers by Department
description_markdown: Department hiring success: For each department with job offers, count total offers extended (`COUNT(jo.offer_id)` as `total_offers`) and the count of accepted offers (`SUM(CASE WHEN jo.status = 'accepted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` as `accepted_count`). starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT jp.department, COUNT(jo.offer_id) AS total_offers, SUM(CASE WHEN jo.status = 'accepted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS accepted_count FROM job_postings jp JOIN job_offers jo ON jp.posting_id = jo.posting_id GROUP BY jp.department ORDER BY total_offers DESC, jp.department ASC;
solution_explanation: Conditional aggregation quantifying accepted employment offers per department.
hints: Join `job_postings jp` and `job_offers jo`.
Use `SUM(CASE WHEN jo.status = 'accepted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`.

Query: SELECT jp.department, COUNT(jo.offer_id) AS total_offers, SUM(CASE WHEN jo.status = 'accepted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS accepted_count FROM job_postings jp JOIN job_offers jo ON jp.posting_id = jo.posting_id GROUP BY jp.department ORDER BY total_offers DESC, jp.department ASC;

title: Compute Running Cumulative Completed Interview Count
description_markdown: Interview throughput cadence: Compute a running cumulative count of completed interviews chronologically: `COUNT(stage_id) OVER (ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC)` as `cumulative_interviews`. Return `stage_id`, `applicant_id`, `stage_name`, `completed_at`, and `cumulative_interviews`. Order by `completed_at` ASC, `stage_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT stage_id, applicant_id, stage_name, completed_at, COUNT(stage_id) OVER (ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC) AS cumulative_interviews FROM interview_stages ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Running count window function over chronological evaluation timestamps.
hints: Use `COUNT(stage_id) OVER (ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC)`.
Order by `completed_at` ASC, `stage_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT stage_id, applicant_id, stage_name, completed_at, COUNT(stage_id) OVER (ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC) AS cumulative_interviews FROM interview_stages ORDER BY completed_at ASC, stage_id ASC;

title: Compute Salary Band Differential from Department Average
description_markdown: Using `AVG() OVER (PARTITION BY department)`, compute the dollar differential between each role's salary ceiling and its departmental average: `ROUND(base_salary_max - AVG(base_salary_max) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2)` as `salary_diff_from_dept_avg`. Return `posting_id`, `title`, `department`, `base_salary_max`, and `salary_diff_from_dept_avg`. Order by `department` ASC, `base_salary_max` DESC, `posting_id` ASC.
starter_query:

SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT posting_id, title, department, base_salary_max, ROUND(base_salary_max - AVG(base_salary_max) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2) AS salary_diff_from_dept_avg FROM job_postings ORDER BY department ASC, base_salary_max DESC, posting_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Compares individual requisition salaries against the departmental partition mean.
hints: Use `ROUND(base_salary_max - AVG(base_salary_max) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2)`.
Order by `department` ASC, `base_salary_max` DESC, `posting_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT posting_id, title, department, base_salary_max, ROUND(base_salary_max - AVG(base_salary_max) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2) AS salary_diff_from_dept_avg FROM job_postings ORDER BY department ASC, base_salary_max DESC, posting_id ASC;

title: Filter Qualified Candidates Meeting Experience Prerequisites
description_markdown: Screening compliance: Retrieve distinct candidate-job pairings where the applicant meets or exceeds the role's mandatory experience (`a.years_experience >= jp.min_experience_years`). Return `a.applicant_id`, `a.first_name`, `a.last_name`, `jp.title`, `a.years_experience`, and `jp.min_experience_years`. Order by `a.applicant_id` ASC, `jp.title` ASC.
starter_query:

SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT DISTINCT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, jp.title, a.years_experience, jp.min_experience_years FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id JOIN job_postings jp ON i.posting_id = jp.posting_id WHERE a.years_experience >= jp.min_experience_years ORDER BY a.applicant_id ASC, jp.title ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins candidates to their interviewed postings and filters by experience compliance.
hints: Join `applicants`, `interview_stages`, and `job_postings`.
Filter with `WHERE a.years_experience >= jp.min_experience_years`.

Query: SELECT DISTINCT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, jp.title, a.years_experience, jp.min_experience_years FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id JOIN job_postings jp ON i.posting_id = jp.posting_id WHERE a.years_experience >= jp.min_experience_years ORDER BY a.applicant_id ASC, jp.title ASC;

title: Filter Strong Performers Scoring At Least 4 in All Rounds
description_markdown: Elite hiring bar: Identify applicants who scored at least 4 in every single interview stage they took (`MIN(i.interviewer_score) >= 4`). Return `a.applicant_id`, `a.first_name`, `a.last_name`, `COUNT(i.stage_id)` as `stages_completed`, and `MIN(i.interviewer_score)` as `lowest_score`. Order by `stages_completed` DESC, `a.applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, COUNT(i.stage_id) AS stages_completed, MIN(i.interviewer_score) AS lowest_score FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id GROUP BY a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name HAVING MIN(i.interviewer_score) >= 4 ORDER BY stages_completed DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses HAVING MIN(...) >= 4 to assert unanimous high ratings.
hints: Group by `a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name`.
Filter with `HAVING MIN(i.interviewer_score) >= 4`.

Query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, COUNT(i.stage_id) AS stages_completed, MIN(i.interviewer_score) AS lowest_score FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id GROUP BY a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name HAVING MIN(i.interviewer_score) >= 4 ORDER BY stages_completed DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;

title: Calculate Offered Salary Efficiency per Year of Experience
description_markdown: Compensation efficiency: For candidates who received a job offer, calculate offered compensation per year of professional experience: `ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 1.0) / a.years_experience, 2)` as `salary_per_exp_year`. Return `a.applicant_id`, `a.first_name`, `a.years_experience`, `jo.offered_salary`, and `salary_per_exp_year`. Order by `salary_per_exp_year` DESC, `a.applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.years_experience, jo.offered_salary, ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 1.0) / a.years_experience, 2) AS salary_per_exp_year FROM applicants a JOIN job_offers jo ON a.applicant_id = jo.applicant_id ORDER BY salary_per_exp_year DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Divides offer remuneration by candidate tenure.
hints: Join `applicants a` and `job_offers jo`.
Compute `ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 1.0) / a.years_experience, 2)`.

Query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.years_experience, jo.offered_salary, ROUND((jo.offered_salary * 1.0) / a.years_experience, 2) AS salary_per_exp_year FROM applicants a JOIN job_offers jo ON a.applicant_id = jo.applicant_id ORDER BY salary_per_exp_year DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;

solution_explanation: Applies DENSE_RANK window function ordered by salary cap.
hints: Use `DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY base_salary_max DESC)`.

title: Measure Interview Rubric Variance and Rating Spread
description_markdown: Evaluation calibration: For each distinct `stage_name`, calculate total evaluations (`COUNT(stage_id)` as `conducted_count`), lowest score (`MIN(interviewer_score)` as `min_score`), highest score (`MAX(interviewer_score)` as `max_score`), and spread (`(MAX(interviewer_score) - MIN(interviewer_score))` as `score_range`). Return `stage_name`, `conducted_count`, `min_score`, `max_score`, and `score_range`. Order by `conducted_count` DESC, `stage_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT stage_name, COUNT(stage_id) AS conducted_count, MIN(interviewer_score) AS min_score, MAX(interviewer_score) AS max_score, (MAX(interviewer_score) - MIN(interviewer_score)) AS score_range FROM interview_stages GROUP BY stage_name ORDER BY conducted_count DESC, stage_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates min, max, and spread of interview scoring bands.
hints: Group by `stage_name`.
Compute `MAX(interviewer_score) - MIN(interviewer_score)` as `score_range`.

Query: SELECT stage_name, COUNT(stage_id) AS conducted_count, MIN(interviewer_score) AS min_score, MAX(interviewer_score) AS max_score, (MAX(interviewer_score) - MIN(interviewer_score)) AS score_range FROM interview_stages GROUP BY stage_name ORDER BY conducted_count DESC, stage_name ASC;

title: Aggregate Full Recruitment Funnel Conversion by Requisition
description_markdown: Hiring funnel conversion: For each job posting in `job_postings`, count distinct interviewed candidates (`COUNT(DISTINCT i.applicant_id)` as `interviewed_candidates`) and distinct job offers extended (`COUNT(DISTINCT jo.offer_id)` as `offers_extended`). Return `jp.posting_id`, `jp.title`, `interviewed_candidates`, and `offers_extended`. Order by `jp.posting_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT jp.posting_id, jp.title, COUNT(DISTINCT i.applicant_id) AS interviewed_candidates, COUNT(DISTINCT jo.offer_id) AS offers_extended FROM job_postings jp LEFT JOIN interview_stages i ON jp.posting_id = i.posting_id LEFT JOIN job_offers jo ON jp.posting_id = jo.posting_id GROUP BY jp.posting_id, jp.title ORDER BY jp.posting_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Multi-table outer joins aggregating distinct candidates interviewed and offers extended.
hints: Use `LEFT JOIN interview_stages i` and `LEFT JOIN job_offers jo`.

Query: SELECT jp.posting_id, jp.title, COUNT(DISTINCT i.applicant_id) AS interviewed_candidates, COUNT(DISTINCT jo.offer_id) AS offers_extended FROM job_postings jp LEFT JOIN interview_stages i ON jp.posting_id = i.posting_id LEFT JOIN job_offers jo ON jp.posting_id = jo.posting_id GROUP BY jp.posting_id, jp.title ORDER BY jp.posting_id ASC;

title: Audit Interviewed Candidates Not Extended Any Job Offer
description_markdown: Talent pipeline disposition audit: Find applicants who completed at least one interview stage but never received an offer in `job_offers`. Compute their average interview score (`ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2)` as `avg_score`). Return `a.applicant_id`, `a.first_name`, `a.last_name`, and `avg_score`. Order by `avg_score` DESC, `a.applicant_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2) AS avg_score FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id LEFT JOIN job_offers jo ON a.applicant_id = jo.applicant_id WHERE jo.offer_id IS NULL GROUP BY a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name ORDER BY avg_score DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Anti-join on job offers filtering candidate pool to rejected or pending interviewees.
hints: Join `applicants a` and `interview_stages i`, then `LEFT JOIN job_offers jo`.
Filter with `WHERE jo.offer_id IS NULL` and group by candidate.

Query: SELECT a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, ROUND(AVG(i.interviewer_score), 2) AS avg_score FROM applicants a JOIN interview_stages i ON a.applicant_id = i.applicant_id LEFT JOIN job_offers jo ON a.applicant_id = jo.applicant_id WHERE jo.offer_id IS NULL GROUP BY a.applicant_id, a.first_name, a.last_name ORDER BY avg_score DESC, a.applicant_id ASC;
